attribution.note: The sentence is verbatim Ars Technica text (minus 'Futurism reported that'), with an unclosed parenthesis and a trailing line about Gordon's case before Gordon is introduced. This indicates a pasted excerpt of another outlet's reporting, not Marcus's own assertion.

semantics.note: If attributable, the normalisation is faithful: a present-tense count of at least eight wrongful-death suits by survivors of ChatGPT users.

contract.note: Counting distinct pending suits on the post date, where the deceased was a ChatGPT user, is an ordinary reading of 'survivors of lost ChatGPT users'. Excluding the Adams suit without evidence that she used ChatGPT is fair.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report and the apparent source of the words. It credits the count to Futurism with no case list, so it cannot settle which suits qualify. It does confirm the Gray suit exists.
November 2025 motion lists five wrongful-death cases (Raine, Lacey, Shamblin, Enneking, Ceccanti). This is a partial subset, not a January 15 inventory.
Court order shows the Lyons/Soelberg estate suit (Soelberg was the user) and the separate Adams suit. Adams' own ChatGPT use is not shown.
Gray complaint establishes Gordon's ChatGPT use and a wrongful-death claim, so it is one qualifying case. Its event_date (2023) is when his use began; the complaint was signed in January 2026.

reviews.rationale: The words appear to be quoted from Ars Technica (itself citing Futurism), not asserted by Marcus, so the attribution is broken. On the merits, the packet establishes seven qualifying suits (Raine, Lacey, Shamblin, Fox/Ceccanti, Enneking, Lyons/Soelberg, Gray/Gordon) and no eighth. With no comprehensive inventory, the contradiction condition is not met either, so the merits would be unresolved.
reviews.abstain_reason: Statement appears misattributed: the verbatim text is a pasted excerpt of Ars Technica reporting attributed to Futurism, not words Marcus wrote and endorsed as his own.
